# Jubilees Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Adam and Eve in Eden; The Fall; The Law of Purification

---

**3:1** On the six days of the second week we brought before Adam, according to the word of God, all the beasts and all the cattle and all the birds and everything that moves on the earth and everything that moves in the water, according to their kinds and according to their types: the beasts on the first day, the cattle on the second day, the birds on the third day, all that moves on the earth on the fourth day, and that which moves in the water on the fifth day.

**3:2** And Adam gave names to all of them; as he called each one, so became its name.

**3:3** On these five days Adam surveyed all of them, but no helper suitable for him was found.

**3:4** Then the LORD said to us: "It is not good for man to be alone; let us make a helper suited to him."

**3:5** The LORD our God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him. While he slept, God took one rib from among his ribs — that rib was the origin of the woman, from his bones — and he closed up the flesh in its place and fashioned the woman.

**3:6** He awakened Adam from his sleep. When he awoke on the sixth day and God brought her to him, Adam knew her and said to her: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken from Man."

**3:7** "Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall be one flesh."

**3:8** In the first week Adam was created, and in the second week the rib — his wife. After this, for the first time, he came to her. In this manner the commandment was given: for purification, seven days for a male child, and twice seven days for a female child.

**3:9** After Adam had spent forty days in the land where he was created, we brought him into the garden of Eden to work it and keep it. His wife was brought in on the eightieth day, and only after this did she enter the garden of Eden.

**3:10** For this reason the commandment is written on the heavenly tablets concerning any woman who gives birth: if she bears a male child, she shall remain in her uncleanness for seven days according to the first week of days, and for thirty-three days she shall remain in the blood of her purification; she shall not touch any holy thing nor enter the sanctuary until those days commanded for a male child are completed.

**3:11** But if she bears a female child, she shall remain in her uncleanness for two weeks of days according to the first two weeks, and sixty-six days in the blood of her purification; in all, eighty days.

**3:12** When Eve had completed these eighty days, we brought her into the garden of Eden, for it is holier than all the rest of the earth, and every tree planted in it is holy.

**3:13** Therefore it was ordained that the woman who bears a male or female child shall not touch any holy thing and shall not enter the sanctuary until these days are fulfilled for the male or female.

**3:14** This is the law and the testimony written down for Israel on the heavenly tablets, that they should observe it all their days.

**3:15** In the first week of the first jubilee, Adam and his wife lived in the garden of Eden for seven years, tilling and keeping it. We gave them work and instructed them in all that is right for cultivation.

**3:16** He tilled the garden and was naked, yet did not know it and was not ashamed. He protected the garden from birds, beasts, and cattle; he gathered its fruit, ate, and set aside the remainder for himself and his wife.

**3:17** After the completion of exactly seven years there, in the second month on the seventeenth day, the serpent came and approached the woman and said to her: "Has God said to you: 'You shall not eat of every tree of the garden'?"

**3:18** She answered: "Of the fruit of all the trees of the garden God has told us: 'Eat.' But of the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden God has told us: 'You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.'"

**3:19** The serpent said to her: "You will certainly not die, for God knows that on the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."

**3:20** The woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom. She took of its fruit and ate, covered her shame with fig leaves, and gave some to her husband, and he ate.

**3:21** His eyes were opened and he saw that he was naked.

**3:22** He took fig leaves, sewed them together, and made a covering for himself to hide his shame.

**3:23** God cursed the serpent and was angry with it forever, and with the woman as well. He was also angry with Adam because he had listened to his wife's voice and eaten from the tree about which God had commanded him not to eat.

**3:24** He drove them out of the garden of Eden. And from that day he commanded us to station the turning sword at the eastern side of the garden of Eden to guard the way to the tree of life.

**3:25** On that day, as Adam went out from the garden of Eden, he offered a sweet-smelling offering: frankincense, galbanum, stacte, and spices, in the morning with the rising of the sun, from the day when he covered his shame.

**3:26** On that day the mouths of all the beasts, the cattle, the birds, and of everything that walks and everything that moves were shut, so that they could no longer speak; for they had all been speaking with one another with one mouth and one tongue.

**3:27** He sent out of the garden of Eden all flesh that was in it, and all flesh was scattered according to its kinds and its types to the places created for each.

**3:28** To Adam alone among all beasts and cattle he gave the capacity to cover his shame.

**3:29** On this account it is prescribed on the heavenly tablets, for all who know the judgment of the law, that they are to cover their shame and not go uncovered as the Gentiles do.

**3:30** On the new moon of the fourth month, Adam and his wife went forth from the land of Eden and lived in the land of Elda, in the land of their creation.

**3:31** And Adam called his wife's name Eve.

**3:32** They had no child until the first jubilee; and after this he was intimate with her.

---
*LOGOS notes: The purification law (vv.8-14) explicitly grounds Lev 12 in Edenic typology: Adam's 40-day solitude → 7+33 male days; Eve's 80-day waiting → 14+66 female days. "Heavenly tablets" (vv.10,14) = Jubilees' meta-Torah. V.26: pre-fall universal animal speech is a distinctive Jubilees motif.*
